about.title: Solana Beach Car Accident Claims
about.longDescription: Solana Beach is a small coastal community, but its roads carry a lot of traffic where I-5 meets Lomas Santa Fe Drive and Rt 101. Public records show 49 injury collisions and 72 injured people in the most recent finalized year, with crashes tending to cluster on Thursday afternoons between 3 and 5 p.m. — likely tied to commute and weekend-getaway timing. If you were injured in one of these collisions, the days right after the crash matter. Insurance companies move fast, and what you say to an adjuster or how quickly evidence disappears can shape your options later. LawProactive doesn't practice law — we connect you, free of charge, with an independent personal injury attorney who can evaluate your situation and explain what California law allows. There's no upfront cost, and attorneys in our network only get paid if you recover something. Reaching out early gives you a better sense of where you actually stand.

whyChoose.title: What Matters Most After a Solana Beach Crash

items.title: California's Clock Is Already Running
items.desc: You generally have two years from the crash date to file a car accident claim in California, but if a government vehicle or road defect was involved, that window can shrink to as little as six months. Getting an attorney involved sooner rather than later helps make sure that deadline never becomes the reason a valid claim gets closed.

items.title: Comparative Fault Doesn't Have to Sink Your Claim
items.desc: California uses a pure comparative fault rule, meaning you can still recover damages even if you're found partly responsible for the crash — your share of fault simply reduces the amount. That makes it important to have someone push back if an insurer tries to pin more blame on you than the facts support.

items.title: No Recorded Statement Without Guidance
items.desc: Insurance adjusters often ask for a recorded statement quickly, before you've had time to think it through — and there's no cap on non-economic damages like pain and suffering in California, so what you say early can matter a lot later. An independent attorney can talk you through what to share and what to hold off on.

items.question: I was hurt in a crash near the I-5 and Lomas Santa Fe Drive area — what should I do first?
items.answer: Get medical attention documented as soon as possible, even if injuries seem minor at first, since some symptoms show up later. Try to preserve any photos, witness names, or dashcam footage before they're lost. Avoid giving a recorded statement to the other driver's insurer until you've spoken with an attorney, since anything you say can be used to reduce your claim.

items.question: Does it cost anything to get connected with an attorney through LawProactive?
items.answer: No. LawProactive is a free connection service — we don't charge you anything to be matched with an independent attorney. Attorneys in our network work on contingency, meaning they only get paid if your case results in a recovery.

items.question: The other driver's insurance company keeps calling me. Do I have to talk to them?
items.answer: You're not required to give a recorded statement to another driver's insurance company, and it's often better not to until you understand your position. Adjusters are trained to ask questions that can minimize what they owe. An independent attorney can communicate with them on your behalf so you don't have to navigate it alone.
